relevance_reason: Case report of a Japanese patient with Cole-Carpenter syndrome type 2 who carries compound heterozygous SEC24D variants.

findings.statement: Takeyari et al. (2018) described a 15-year-old Japanese boy with Cole-Carpenter syndrome. He had short-trunk short stature and craniofacial abnormalities, including ocular proptosis, marked frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, and micrognathia. He also had low bone mineral density and basilar impression.
quotes: We describe a 15-year-old Japanese boy with short stature of the short-trunk type and craniofacial abnormalities including ocular proptosis, marked frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, and micrognathia.
He had low-bone mineral density and basilar impression.

phenotypes.text: short stature of the short-trunk type

findings.statement: Takeyari et al. (2018) used whole exome sequencing to identify compound heterozygous variants in the SEC24D gene, p.Arg484* and p.Arg313His, in a Japanese boy with Cole-Carpenter syndrome type 2.
quotes: Whole exome sequencing analysis identified biallelic variants in SEC24D (p.Arg484* and p.Arg313His) in the patient.
We will report a patient with compound heterozygous variants of SEC24D causing Cole-Carpenter syndrome type 2.

relevance_reason: The paper reports Chinese patients with compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations who have recessive OI with craniofacial ossification defects, which is the SEC24D-related phenotype (Cole-Carpenter syndrome 2).

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2017) described a 23-year-old Chinese man (family 1) with recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta, an open anterior fontanel, and facial dysmorphism. CT 3-dimensional imaging of the cranium showed skull deformities with a broad ossification defect in the frontoapical area, a widened sagittal suture, and wormian bones.
quotes: In family 1, the proband was a 23-year-old male; he had recurrent fractures and dentinogenesis imperfecta. His anterior fontanel was not closed, and he showed facial dysmorphism.

A computed tomography three-dimensional imaging of the cranium showed skull deformities associated with a broad ossification defect in the frontoapical area, a widened sagittal suture, and Wormian bones.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2017) described a 7-year-old Chinese boy (family 2) who had recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta, and an open anterior fontanel, but no obvious facial dysmorphism.
quotes: In family 2, the proband was a 7-year-old boy, who also had recurrent fractures and dentinogenesis imperfecta. His anterior fontanel was not closed, and he did not have obvious facial dysmorphism.

findings.statement: Using whole-exome sequencing in the proband from family 1, Zhang et al. (2017) identified novel compound heterozygous missense mutations in the SEC24D gene: c.2723G>A (p.Cys908Tyr) and c.2842T>C (p.Ser948Pro).
quotes: We identified one novel compound heterozygous missense substitution in the proband in family 1, including c.2723G>A (p. Cys908Tyr) and c.2842T>C (p. Ser948Pro).
Using whole-exome sequencing in two probands, we identified two novel compound heterozygous mutations in SEC24D.

findings.statement: Using whole-exome sequencing in the proband from family 2, Zhang et al. (2017) identified novel compound heterozygous missense mutations in the SEC24D gene: c.938G>A (p.Arg313His) and c.875C>T (p.Pro292Leu).
quotes: In the proband in family 2, we identified another novel compound heterozygous missense substitution, including c.938G>A (p. Arg313His) and c.875C>T (p. Pro292Leu).

relevance_reason: The title reports that SEC24D mutations cause autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta. SEC24D is the gene for Cole-Carpenter syndrome 2. Only the title was available, so no detail about patients or variants can be extracted.

findings.statement: Moosa et al. (2016) reported that mutations in the SEC24D gene cause autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
quotes: Mutations in SEC24D cause autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.

relevance_reason: This paper first reported SEC24D mutations as the cause of a syndromic osteogenesis imperfecta resembling Cole-Carpenter syndrome. It describes the affected patients, their variants and functional studies in their cells.

findings.statement: Garbes et al. (2015) reported 3 affected individuals from 2 families who had a similar skeletal phenotype: a 7-year-old boy whose phenotype most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome, and 2 fetuses first suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta. All 3 had severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures beginning before birth. The boy also had short stature and craniofacial malformations, including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing and down-slanting palpebral fissures.
quotes: The affected individuals were a 7-year-old boy with a phenotype most closely resembling Cole-Carpenter syndrome and two fetuses initially suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta.
All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset.
The 7-year-old boy had short stature and craniofacial malformations including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing, and down-slanting palpebral fissures.

phenotypes.text: severely disturbed ossification of the skull

findings.statement: Garbes et al. (2015) used whole-exome sequencing to find 3 mutant SEC24D alleles in 3 affected individuals from 2 families. Each affected individual was compound heterozygous for 2 of these alleles. SEC24D encodes a component of the COPII complex, which is involved in protein export from the endoplasmic reticulum.
quotes: As a result of a whole-exome sequencing study, we report three mutant alleles in SEC24D, a gene encoding a component of the COPII complex involved in protein export from the ER
Three individuals from two families affected by a similar skeletal phenotype were each compound heterozygous for two of these mutant alleles

findings.statement: Garbes et al. (2015) identified a c.3044C>T missense mutation in SEC24D, causing a p.Ser1015Phe substitution in a cargo-binding pocket. It was found in the compound heterozygous state in all 3 affected individuals from 2 families. The variant lay within a 14-Mb founder haplotype shared by all 3 individuals.
quotes: the missense mutations c.3044C>T (p.Ser1015Phe, located in a cargo-binding pocket)
with c.3044C>T being embedded in a 14 Mb founder haplotype shared by all three

findings.statement: Garbes et al. (2015) identified a c.613C>T truncating mutation in SEC24D, resulting in p.Gln205Ter. Patients carried it in the compound heterozygous state together with another SEC24D mutation.
quotes: the truncating mutation c.613C>T (p.Gln205(∗))

findings.statement: Garbes et al. (2015) identified a c.2933A>C missense mutation in SEC24D, causing a p.Gln978Pro substitution in the gelsolin-like domain. Patients carried it in the compound heterozygous state together with another SEC24D mutation.
quotes: c.2933A>C (p.Gln978Pro, located in the gelsolin-like domain)

findings.statement: Garbes et al. (2015) examined skin fibroblasts from the affected boy using electron and immunofluorescence microscopy. Export of procollagen from the endoplasmic reticulum was inefficient and the ER tubules were dilated, reproducing the cellular phenotype seen in cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia caused by SEC23A mutations. The authors noted that the cellular and morphologic phenotypes matched those described in Sec24d-deficient fish mutants: vbi (medaka) and bulldog (zebrafish).
quotes: Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy of skin fibroblasts of this individual revealed that ER export of procollagen was inefficient and that ER tubules were dilated, faithfully reproducing the cellular phenotype of individuals with cranio-lentico-sutural dysplasia (CLSD).
The cellular and morphological phenotypes we report are in concordance with the phenotypes described for the Sec24d-deficient fish mutants vbi (medaka) and bulldog (zebrafish).

findings.statement: Garbes et al. (2015) noted that cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia, caused by SEC23A mutations, has a largely overlapping craniofacial phenotype. Unlike the SEC24D disorder, however, it does not feature generalized bone fragility, and the original family described had cataracts.
quotes: CLSD is caused by SEC23A mutations and displays a largely overlapping craniofacial phenotype, but it is not characterized by generalized bone fragility and presented with cataracts in the original family described.
